history.period: 1666 (birth of Guru Gobind Singh, 22 December 1666); rebuilt 1839 by Maharaja Ranjit Singh after a fire; rebuilt 1948-1957 (Rs 20 lakh) after the 1934 earthquake
history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Takht Sri Patna Sahib, also called Takhat Sri Harimandir Ji, is one of the five Takhts (seats of authority) of Sikhism, built at the birthplace of the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, in Patna City. A devotee of Guru Nanak, Salis Rai Johri, converted his haveli into a dharamshala here, where Guru Tegh Bahadur also stayed. The building was rebuilt by Maharaja Ranjit Singh in 1839 after a fire, and again in 1948-1957 (Rs 20 lakh) after damage in the 1934 Bihar earthquake. It houses relics of the Guru — handwritten hukamnamas, weapons, iron arrows, an ivory-handled sword, a gold-plated cradle — plus a museum. Guru Nanak and Guru Tegh Bahadur also visited Patna.

name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
town_description: Patna is the capital of Bihar and one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities (ancient Pataliputra), set on the southern bank of the Ganga. Its old-city quarter, Patna City, holds the Takht on Harmandir Gali near the riverbank.
